content:
maya: Heads up — Customer Acme (account acct_AMA) escalated. After last night's runtime rollout p95 for their /v1/chat completion path jumped from ~220ms to ~820ms and p99 is ~2.3s. They do a lot of function/tool-calling with structured JSON outputs. They say it started right after deploy. attaching a short sample from their call sequence.

oliver: Can you paste a simple repro? is this hosted or dedicated?

maya: Hosted. Minimal repro they gave: chat -> tool_router -> call /price_tool (sync) -> structured output validation against schema. They reported extra ~400ms per request.

anika: I saw a related alert on the router service around 02:14 UTC — spike in tail latency. p95 for router went from 50ms to 420ms. p99 from 120ms to 2s.

sre-oncall: I pulled traces. Most added time is in tool-router.service -> validate_schema() and then in the sync HTTP client to the tool (though the HTTP call itself is ~80-120ms). validate_schema is showing CPU spikes on the node making validation synchronously before enqueuing tool call.

sam: Which validation code is running? We have two paths: strict-jsonschema (python jsonschema library) and fast-schema-check (Rust wasm executor). The rollout switched default to strict-jsonschema for a subset of customers to avoid silent coercions.

oliver: that sounds like it. Strict-jsonschema is heavy if we run it per-request without caching. it does deep validation and formats errors.

maya: Customer confirmed they supply a large nested schema (~45 fields, nested objects + arrays). Tool router runs validate then run_tool.

anika: repro steps I used locally:
```bash
# reproduce locally with our load script
python tools/repro_toolcall.py --host api.redwood.test --concurrency 8 --profile acme_schema.json
```
Observed: baseline with fast-schema-check: p95 ~210ms; with strict-jsonschema: p95 ~760ms.
```
# quick flamegraph on router node
ssh router-2
sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
```

sam: output of `strace` suggests long syscalls during Python validation (malloc + recursion).

oliver: mitigation ideas:
- revert strict-jsonschema default to fast-schema-check for hosted customers (hotfix)
- move validation off the hot-path: accept tool call, return immediate 202, validate async and call tool when validated (breaking change, needs API discussion)
- cache validation result per (schema_hash, model+route) for N minutes
- short-circuit schema validation for simple types (strings/numbers)

anika: short term we can flip flag for Acme to fast-schema-check. I can push a config change.

maya: please do. Also customer asked for root cause and timeline. we should provide numbers pre/post.

deploy-bot: deploy  -> routers:toggle-validation-mode for account acct_AMA scheduled by anika at 2026-03-15T08:12:00Z

sre-oncall: toggled flag on routing layer for acct_AMA. Observing telemetry: p95 dropped from 820ms -> 240ms in 3 minutes. p99 down to ~450ms. still slightly above pre-deploy but much better.

oliver: Good. Longer term we need a safe default. Sam, can we optimize strict-jsonschema? Maybe compile to Wasm and run in a threadpool?

sam: yes. two engineering tasks: 1) compile strict rules to Rust/WASM and run in the fast executor (should cut CPU 3-5x). 2) add LRU cache keyed by schema_hash + route_signature. I can do #2 quickly (1-2 days). #1 will need design + perf tests (2-3 weeks).

anika: also recommend we instrument tool-router to emit per-step latencies (validate, serialize, http-call, parse) per request id. add a short label when schema size > X to help SLO dashboards.

maya: action items for customer reply:
- summary: temporary mitigation applied (validation mode set to "fast" for acct_AMA). p95/p99 significantly improved.
- next steps: we will add cache and optimize strict validator; timeline: cache in 48h, wasm validator in ~3w.
- ask: can they share a sanitized sample payload and schema to test against?

oliver: logging/trace snippet to include in reply:
```
router.request_id=2jk3bfa validate_time=392ms parse_time=10ms http_call=95ms tool_duration=48ms total=545ms
```

support-bot: Created ticket INC-5421 (Priority P2) and github issue GH-1234 (runtime/validation perf). Linked to customer acct_AMA.

sam: I added a quick LRU cache PR in draft: `pr/validation-cache`. It caches schema_hash -> compiled_validator for 5m. Reduces validate_time from ~360ms -> 12ms in local.

anika: after enabling cache for acct_AMA on staging, p95 dropped to 260ms and p99 to 480ms. rolling to prod for account after approval.

maya: thanks team. Customer update going out in ~30m with timeline + repro ask. We should also add a postmortem note linking this thread and INC-5421.

oliver: postmortem points: cause = defaulting a subset of customers to strict-jsonschema during rollback/rollout, poor visibility of per-step latencies, missing caching for schema validators. mitigation = toggle, cache, wasm optimization, add per-step metrics + alerts.

sam: GH-1234 includes perfbench scripts and sample schemas. I'll add the customer sample once they approve.

maya: leaving this open until cache is live for acct_AMA and GH-1234 has an initial plan. updating INC-5421 with timelines.

support-bot: INC-5421 status updated: mitigation applied -> partial, next action: validation-cache rollout.

sre-oncall: follow-up: make sure router autoscaling policies cover CPU spikes from validation (node CPU went to 92%). Might want to add fast-path CPU reservation.

oliver: noted. I'll add autoscale rule change to GH-1234 as a separate subtask.

maya: thanks all — I'll send the customer note now and link this thread.
